themes_detail.label: Street Signs Failing Across District
themes_detail.summary: Dangling and damaged street signs spiked dramatically THIS WEEK with 5 dangling complaints (vs. 0.4 weekly average) and 5 damaged complaints last week (vs. 0.9 weekly average), creating potential safety hazards for pedestrians and drivers across Park Slope.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average (1233% spike, z-score: 9.55)
Street Sign - Damaged: 5 complaints last week vs 0.9 weekly average (471% spike, z-score: 4.45)
Combined 10 sign complaints over past 8 days suggests infrastructure maintenance failure or weather event impact
reporting_angles: Walk key intersections (Prospect Park West, 7th Ave, Flatbush) to document hanging/damaged signs and assess public safety risk
Request DOT maintenance records: when was last sign inspection in CD306? What triggered this spike?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Pile Up on Streets
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, a 522% increase over the 1.1 weekly average, indicating either a surge in bike dumping or enforcement of abandoned vehicle removal.
evidence: Abandoned Bike complaints: 7 THIS WEEK vs 1.1 weekly average (522% spike, z-score: 5.58)
No prior spike pattern in 8-week baseline suggests acute, recent trigger
Aligns with city-wide bike-share and micro-mobility growth pressures
reporting_angles: Map the 7 complaints: are they clustered near transit hubs (Prospect Park, F-train)? Suggests specific hotspot
Investigate: new bike-share operator in area, or intensified city enforcement of 311-flagged abandoned bikes?

themes_detail.label: Trees Dying, Branches Overgrown
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked 1100% two weeks ago (3 vs 0.2 weekly average), and overgrown tree/branch complaints jumped 367% last week (7 vs 1.5 weekly average), suggesting accelerating tree health crisis or deferred maintenance in parks and streets.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Overgrown Tree/Branches: 7 complaints last week vs 1.5 weekly average (367% spike, z-score: 4.49)
10 tree-related complaints in past 9 days; aligns with CB budget request for park reconstruction/upgrades suggesting chronic neglect
reporting_angles: Visit Prospect Park and residential streets: document specific dying/overgrown trees, interview residents about safety concerns (falling branches)
Request Parks Dept data: tree trimming schedule for CD306 last 6 months; has maintenance been deferred or accelerated?

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints jumped 460% last week with 7 complaints vs. 1.2 weekly average, suggesting either a wave of illegal conversions, overcrowding, or enforcement activity in Park Slope.
evidence: Building/Use complaints: 7 last week vs 1.2 weekly average (460% spike, z-score: 4.43)
1,141 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (703 alterations), suggesting active renovation/conversion activity
Aligns with CB budget request for zoning study to address affordable housing needs and land-use pressures
reporting_angles: Subpoena DOB inspection reports: which buildings triggered the 7 violations last week? Illegal units, overcrowding, or unsafe alterations?
Interview CB District Manager and elected officials: are they seeing uptick in landlord-driven conversions (basement units, room subdivisions) amid housing pressure?

themes_detail.label: Dumpster Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints surged 200% three weeks ago with 6 complaints vs. 2.0 weekly average, indicating potential waste management or illegal dumping issues in the district.
evidence: Dumpster Complaint: 6 complaints 3 weeks ago vs 2.0 weekly average (200% spike, z-score: 4.0)
Spike occurred 3 weeks ago; no recent acceleration suggests issue may be resolving or was localized
reporting_angles: DSNY records: were there service delays or route changes 3-4 weeks ago in CD306?
Canvas areas with high complaints: illegal dumping on residential blocks, overflowing commercial dumpsters?
